name: Humerus Trochlea Aplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Humerus Trochlea Aplasia

criteria.description: Radiological absence of the humeral trochlea on elbow imaging
Clinical evidence of elbow joint instability or abnormal range of motion
Congenital malformation of the elbow without other skeletal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiological absence of the humeral trochlea plus clinical signs of elbow joint instability
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and clinical examination; genetic testing may be supportive if available.

searchTerms: absence of humeral trochlea at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elbow joint instability due to trochlear aplasia
searchTerms: unstable elbow joint from missing bone
elbow joint looseness due to bone absence
elbow instability caused by trochlear aplasia

common.symptomName: Limited elbow flexion and extension range
searchTerms: limited bending and straightening of elbow
difficulty fully flexing or extending elbow

common.symptomName: Abnormal carrying angle of the elbow
Mild elbow deformity apparent at birth
searchTerms: slight elbow deformity present at birth
small elbow shape difference from birth

common.symptomName: Joint laxity localized to the elbow

searchTerms: recurrent elbow slipping out of place

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones related to upper limb function
searchTerms: slow development of upper limb skills
radial head slipping out of place

rare.symptomName: Secondary osteoarthritic changes in the elbow joint
searchTerms: joint wear and tear in elbow

rare.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms due to joint instability
searchTerms: nerve compression due to elbow looseness
tingling or numbness from joint instability

imaging: Absence of the humeral trochlea on X-ray or MRI
Elbow joint instability visualized on dynamic imaging
Possible radial head subluxation or dislocation
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible sporadic or familial cases reported
other: Clinical examination revealing abnormal elbow joint mechanics

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of radial head dislocation without trochlear aplasia
Generalized elbow joint malformations involving multiple structures
May include humeral condyle abnormalities beyond trochlea

redFlags: Severe elbow instability causing functional impairment
Progressive joint deformity or worsening range of motion
